## Verdict

Inkwell costs least for a team of 22, at $242 per month. Its 20-seat minimum sits below the team size, so all 22 seats bill at the list rate of $11. Dorado is next at $528, and Borealis is the most expensive at $600 despite a mid-range seat price, because its 40-seat minimum forces payment for 18 seats the team will not use.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $24 | 5 |
| Inkwell | $11 | 20 |
| Borealis | $15 | 40 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (22) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Dorado:** minimum 5 is below 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $24 = **$528 per month**.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 20 is below 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $11 = **$242 per month**.
- **Borealis:** minimum 40 exceeds 22, so 40 seats paid. 40 × $15 = **$600 per month**. Eighteen seats, worth $270, go unused.

Inkwell is $286 per month cheaper than Dorado and $358 cheaper than Borealis — $3,432 and $4,296 over twelve months.

## Risks

The ranking is stable as the team grows but not as it shrinks. Inkwell's 20-seat floor means a drop to 18 people still bills $220, while Dorado at 18 people costs $432 and only becomes cheaper than Inkwell's floor below 9 seats. Borealis holds at $600 until headcount reaches 40, at which point Inkwell costs $440 — so Borealis does not overtake Inkwell at any size here.

This compares price and nothing else. The list carries no feature, support, security or usage-limit detail, so a cheaper seat may buy a smaller product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments, volume discounts, onboarding and migration costs are absent from the source and could reorder the result. Confirm whether minimums bind at signup or only at renewal.
